sources.title: ITU-T X.200 (07/1994): Information technology — Open Systems Interconnection — Basic Reference Model: The basic model
sources.supportedClaim: Physical entities transmit bits over physical media and can relay interconnected circuits; transmission may be synchronous or asynchronous.
sources.limits: Conceptual architecture only. No universal medium, numeric threshold, wire header, or claim that PHYs never have their own error mechanisms.
sources.inspection: Opened official recommendation, followed English PDF, inspected section text

sources.title: RFC 1122: Requirements for Internet Hosts — Communication Layers
sources.supportedClaim: The Internet suite distinguishes application, transport, Internet and link functions; its grouping differs from the OSI teaching realms.
sources.limits: Historical architectural context, not current protocol configuration guidance; does not authorize seven invented mandatory headers.
sources.inspection: Opened RFC Editor HTML and read corresponding publisher plain-text section

sources.title: Cisco 800 Series Integrated Services Router Hardware Installation Guide — Technical Specifications
sources.section: Cable Specifications → Ethernet Cable Specifications → Maximum Cable Length
sources.supportedClaim: This hardware guide specifies a 100 m maximum Ethernet cable distance between the described router and connected equipment.
sources.limits: Product-specific illustration only. The game 100 m channel and inclusive comparator remain fictional; no universal limit for all copper or all Ethernet. No certification claim.
sources.inspection: Opened publisher page with browser tool

sources.title: What's Wrong with My Cable?
sources.section: Failures of the Five Wiremap Tests
sources.supportedClaim: Wiremap examines conductor continuity and termination; an open can reflect a broken conductor, poor connection or damaged connector.
sources.limits: The fixture supplies a diagnosed required-path break. An arbitrary open indication alone does not prove its location or cause; tester setup also matters.
sources.inspection: Opened publisher page with browser tool

sources.title: IBM AS/400e series: LAN, Frame-Relay and ATM Support, Version 4, SC41-5404-01
sources.section: Chapter 5 Ethernet networks → Ethernet topologies → Repeater hubs; PDF page 101
sources.supportedClaim: Historical Ethernet repeater hubs receive and repeat data to linked segments with amplification and retiming; the described shared medium operates half duplex.
sources.limits: Not a modern wireless extender or a universal repeater topology allowance. Inability to restore an unchanged physical break is an explicit scenario inference, supported together with S04.
sources.inspection: Opened IBM PDF; downloaded to temporary directory and extracted the exact page using pdftotext; no source copy retained

sources.title: QFX5130 Network Cable and Transceiver Planning
sources.section: Calculate Power Budget and Power Margin for Fiber-Optic Cables → Calculate Power Budget for Fiber-Optic Cables; How to Calculate Power Margin for Fiber-Optic Cables
sources.supportedClaim: Budget equals minimum transmit power minus receiver sensitivity; margin subtracts link loss from that budget. Actual component losses need vendor data.
sources.limits: Original Juniper URL redirects to publisher HPE documentation. Use equations only; a positive margin does not independently prove the maximum receiver bound. No sample losses or fixture thresholds imported.
sources.inspection: Opened Juniper URL/redirect; read equation text in returned publisher HTML

sources.title: Cisco 10GBASE SFP+ Modules Data Sheet
sources.section: Platform support; Product specifications, Table 3 SFP+ port cabling specifications and Table 4 Optical transmit and receive specifications
sources.supportedClaim: Module-specific media, wavelength, reach and receiver minimum/maximum power are separate specifications. Host compatibility requires support information.
sources.limits: No real module is instantiated in the toy optical fixture. Do not generalize shell shape or SMF/MMF slogans; supported combinations vary by module.
sources.inspection: Opened publisher page and read Table 4 rows in publisher HTML

sources.title: Troubleshooting a Traditional Cisco Wireless Network
sources.section: Check Physical and Environmental Conditions; Run Connectivity Tests from the Web User Interface; Radio Settings; Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR)
sources.supportedClaim: Power, cable attachment, link indication, obstructions/range and connectivity tests are distinct observations; radio settings and noise affect diagnosis.
sources.limits: Product troubleshooting context, not universal SNR or throughput guarantees. Do not import configuration recommendations, channel legality, security or service success into the toy profile.
sources.inspection: Opened publisher page with browser tool

sources.title: Wireless Site Survey FAQ
sources.supportedClaim: SNR is a signal-to-noise power ratio; its dB value is ten times the base-ten logarithm of that ratio.
sources.limits: For compatible power measurements with one reference, subtracting dBm yields dB. No universal acceptable threshold follows from this definition.
sources.inspection: Opened publisher page with browser tool

sources.title: Power over Ethernet (PoE) standards and compatibility
sources.section: Introductory PSE/PD definitions; PoE budget; PoE class, table headings for power delivered to PD versus switch-port output
sources.supportedClaim: PSE output and power delivered to a PD are distinct accounting boundaries. Multiple devices must fit the available aggregate budget.
sources.limits: Only this distinction and aggregate-budget concept are used. No table wattages, PoE class allocation, priority behavior or detection timing are used by the fiction.
sources.inspection: Opened publisher page with browser tool

sources.title: Configure and Verify Ethernet 10/100/1000Mb Half/Full Duplex Auto-Negotiation
sources.section: When to Use Ethernet 10/100 Mb Auto-Negotiation
sources.supportedClaim: Negotiation exchanges supported speed and duplex abilities; both link partners need coherent settings.
sources.limits: T11 is set intersection with one common member and both ends negotiating. Forced modes, parallel detection and modern PHY-specific negotiation are outside this model.
sources.inspection: Opened publisher page with browser tool

sources.title: AN 835: PAM4 Signaling Fundamentals — 2.1 Naming Conventions
sources.section: 2.1 Naming Conventions; Table 4 Linear and Gray Coding
sources.supportedClaim: Four amplitude levels can represent four two-bit combinations; the source distinguishes linear and Gray coding.
sources.limits: T12 deliberately uses the declared linear toy labels. Do not substitute a real PHY map, count useful bitrate from symbol count, or imply the toy implements PAM4.
sources.inspection: Opened publisher page with browser tool

sources.title: AN 835: PAM4 Signaling Fundamentals — 4.2.3 Clock and Data Recovery (CDR)
sources.supportedClaim: High-speed serial reception includes clock/data recovery; multilevel signaling requires appropriate timing recovery.
sources.limits: Physical timing context only. The toy uses explicit discrete sampling; no analog jitter model, NTP synchronization, timing reflex requirement or CDR implementation.
sources.inspection: Opened publisher page with browser tool

assumptions: Known compatible endpoints/media/terminations; one passive channel; supplied lengths exact and nonnegative.
Every required conductor is continuous unless explicitly broken; fresh tests required.
limits: No cable certification, electromagnetic model, hidden permanent-link/patch-cord sublimits or real-product claim.
Repeater added without fixing a break cannot restore continuity. Regenerative topologies require separate reviewed segment limits and are unsupported here.

assumptions: Explicit matched pair, media, wavelength direction, supported rate, connector/polarity and host capability; inspected connection.
Loss is passive, finite and nonnegative, expressed in dB; total provided includes all modeled losses; no amplifier.
limits: No dispersion, uncertainty, aging, temperature or actual product simulation.
T06 supplies received power independently; combining 0 dBm receive with -3 dBm transmit and nonnegative passive loss is inconsistent content.

assumptions: Signal and noise use comparable received power measurements in dBm.
Known compatible radio settings and viable path are independently supplied; sample fresh after change.
limits: No universal Wi-Fi throughput, channel ranking, coverage model or regulatory assertion.
Missing authored path/settings facts are content-error; explicitly incompatible chosen settings are incorrect.

assumptions: Budget and demands measured at the delivered endpoint boundary after losses.
Device/port/power-method compatibility and per-port constraints independently satisfied.
limits: No PoE class, voltage negotiation, inrush model or hidden PSE-to-PD loss subtraction.
Power adequacy alone does not prove data connectivity.

assumptions: Both endpoints negotiate; accepted selection must exist in both advertised sets.
T11 has one common member, so no ranking algorithm is needed.
limits: No unsupported capability creation, forced-mode fallback, parallel detection, PAUSE or master/slave simulation.
A challenge with several common choices must declare and review any ranking rule; do not invent one.

assumptions: Discrete exact samples are provided in order with explicit sample positions; player may step, pause and replay.
limits: No analog voltage claim, complete PAM4 PHY, clock-rate/throughput inference or timing score.
Unknown authored symbols/missing sample positions are content-error; missing learner answer is invalid-input.

parameters.displayBitOrder: most-significant-bit first within each highlighted byte

assumptions: Two highlighted bytes within an opaque upper-interface frame; known sample order.
Compare recovered highlighted bits after evaluating the declared physical path.
limits: Display bit order is a toy convention, not a claim about Ethernet serialization.
Not a whole two-byte Ethernet frame, FCS validation, universal error detector or higher-layer simulator.
